Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component's ownership structure: who creates, retains, changes and releases its state, storage and resources, and their lifetimes. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Structure the tree as an ownership decomposition of the core component:
  - Top-level branches are the core's root owners: the long-lived holders from which its other state and resources hang. Each owned thing appears in exactly one place, under its owner.
  - Depth always means "is owned by": a child is created, retained or released by its parent, and does not outlive it unless handed off.
  - Under each owner, state when its children are created, changed and released. Show borrowed or shared references as -> lines to their owner, not as children.
  - Other relationships appear only where they explain a lifetime; do not organize the tree around calls or modules.
Cover breadth before depth:
  - Name every major owner in the core, even in one line, before detailing any of them.
  - When an owner holds substantial state of its own, give it a child line naming what it holds, even if you do not expand it.
  - Do not detail one owner down to field layouts, allocators or buffers while another major owner remains a single line.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title

`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Ghostty terminal-session core: ownership roots and per-pane lifetimes
|
|-- Core App: application-lifetime shared services [src/App.zig:80-156]
|   |-- surfaces registry, focused_surface, mailbox and application flags
|   |   |   Created by App.init; addSurface/deleteSurface change registration;
|   |   |   tick drains messages; App.deinit releases registry storage.
|   |   `-- -> Runtime surface owners below: pointers, not surface allocations.
|   |       deleteSurface does not destroy; App.deinit requests runtime deinit.
|   |-- font_grid_set: font.SharedGridSet [src/font/SharedGridSet.zig:53-168,413]
|   |   |   App.init creates; surfaces acquire references; deref destroys a grid
|   |   |   at zero references. App shutdown expects no remaining grids.
|   |   |-- Font library, discovery state, keyed grid map and synchronization
|   |   |   Created eagerly/lazily by the set; released by SharedGridSet.deinit.
|   |   `-- SharedGrid instances: resolver/font collection, glyph caches, atlases
|   |       Populated during font lookup/rasterization; shared across matching
|   |       surfaces; freed with their grid [src/font/SharedGrid.zig:42-64,122].
|   `-- device: optional renderer.Device [src/Surface.zig:567-575]
|       First Surface.init creates it and stores it in App; all surface renderers
|       borrow it. App.deinit releases it only after surface cleanup.
|
|-- Application runtime: apprt.App / host-controlled application handle
|   |   Startup creates runtime beside Core App; embedded API creates both.
|   |   Runtime termination and Core App destruction are separate operations
|   |   [src/main_ghostty.zig:99-115; src/apprt/embedded.zig:1718-1747].
|   |-- Runtime configuration and application integration state
|   |   |-- Embedded App.config, keymap and callback options
|   |   |   init clones config; keymap initializes lazily; terminate frees config
|   |   |   and keymap [src/apprt/embedded.zig:139-173].
|   |   `-- GTK Application config reference, CSS providers, shortcuts and helpers
|   |       Retained by Application; replaced as settings change; deinit releases
|   |       them [src/apprt/gtk/class/application.zig:264,456-483,1253].
|   `-- -> Core App: runtime core_app points at the shared-services owner above.
|       Config updates are borrowed calls: Core App.updateConfig does not retain
|       the caller's Config; surfaces derive their own state [src/App.zig:172-198].
|
`-- Runtime surface owner: one live terminal pane, controlled by GUI/host
    |   GTK widget initSurface/finalize allocates and destroys CoreSurface;
    |   embedded App.newSurface/freeSurface allocates and frees its wrapper.
    |   These are alternative runtimes, not duplicate terminal instances
    |   [src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:1963-1981,3557-3629;
    |    src/apprt/embedded.zig:280-293,504-645].
    |-- Wrapper-local presentation state
    |   Title/configuration references, platform/input state and optional inspector
    |   presentation live with the wrapper; teardown unregisters the pane before
    |   destroying its core [src/apprt/embedded.zig:451-504,634-645;
    |   src/apprt/gtk/class/surface.zig:585-666,1893-2027].
    |-- -> Application runtime and Core App: borrowed application context;
    |   a live pane needs their configuration, callbacks and shared services.
    `-- core_surface: Surface -- terminal-session coordinator [src/Surface.zig]
        |   init creates session children and spawns renderer/I/O workers.
        |   deinit first stops search, then stops/joins renderer, then I/O;
        |   only afterward does it release shared session storage (477-893).
        |-- Interaction/configuration state: config, mouse, keyboard, size and flags
        |   |   Surface callbacks change focus, visibility, dimensions, selections,
        |   |   bindings and read-only state; updateConfig replaces derived settings.
        |   |   These are pane-local, not application-global (69-188,1804).
        |   |-- DerivedConfig storage, queued key sequences and binding-table stack
        |   |   Built/copied for the surface; changed by configuration/input;
        |   |   released by Surface.deinit (361-442,866-891).
        |   `-- Mouse selection gesture and keyboard/IME bookkeeping
        |       Gesture cleanup occurs before terminal destruction; its tracked
        |       positions refer into -> io.terminal [Surface.deinit:861-864].
        |-- Font reference token: font_grid_key, font_size and font_metrics
        |   Acquired at init; setFontSize acquires a replacement and hands old-key
        |   release to the renderer mailbox. Final token is dereferenced on close
        |   (528-536,881-882,2536-2570).
        |   -> Core App.font_grid_set owns the actual fonts, caches and atlases.
        |-- renderer_state: shared synchronization and presentation state
        |   |   Surface allocates its mutex; updates mouse/preedit state; releases
        |   |   preedit storage and mutex after workers stop (615-621,885-889).
        |   |-- Owned mutex allocation, preedit codepoints, mouse and demand state
        |   |   Readers/writers synchronize terminal access through this mutex
        |   |   [src/renderer/State.zig:17-45].
        |   |-- -> io.terminal: borrowed authoritative terminal, not a second copy.
        |   `-- -> inspector: optional borrowed pointer, detached before destruction.
        |-- io: termio.Termio -- authoritative terminal and backend owner
        |   |   Surface.init transfers backend, derived config and mailbox into io;
        |   |   Termio.deinit releases them after I/O shutdown
        |   |   [src/Surface.zig:693-748; src/termio/Termio.zig:254-367].
        |   |-- terminal: terminal.Terminal [src/terminal/Terminal.zig:49-106,344-403]
        |   |   |   Created at pane dimensions. PTY parsing changes terminal state;
        |   |   |   resize/input actions also mutate it under renderer_state.mutex.
